summary: Wearing a warning ring reaches an unported Ring_on branch. C refreshes monsters and shows a red warning 1 for the level-5 ogre. This shares the Ring_on scope with the orc threshold case.

source.branch: Putting the slot-f RIN_WARNING on the left hand calls see_monsters; warning requires an active property, a hostile nearby monster, and integer monster level / 4 at least context.warnlevel.

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/do_wear.c:1242-1344 defines Ring_on. After clearing wield/quiver references and preserving the other ring property mask, RIN_WARNING calls see_monsters. accessory_or_armor_on at 2209 and its ring branch set the worn slot before calling Ring_on; doputon provides the production command route.

js/do_wear.js:818-823 throws UnsupportedRingOnError for RIN_WARNING instead of calling see_monsters. The admitted baseline stops at the left-hand selection boundary, before the turn completes; the later mcalcmove comparator gap does not diagnose monster movement.

nethack-c/upstream/src/display.c:1487-1522 see_monsters refreshes monster locations and special display state. display_warning at 634-651 uses warning_of unless hallucinating, then show_mon_or_warn. warning_of at 654-662 clamps integer level / 4 to WARNCOUNT - 1.

nethack-c/upstream/include/display.h:64-66 requires Warning, a non-peaceful monster, distance squared below 100, and integer level / 4 >= context.warnlevel. allmain.c:774 initializes warnlevel=1. Existing JS display.js monsterWarnsHero and warning_of mirror this threshold; their declarations do not by themselves establish whole-function completion.

The frozen recording at segment 0 step 54, key l, shows f - a wire ring (on left hand) and red warning glyph 1 by the hero. The invisible hostile ogre has level 5, so 5 / 4 truncates to 1 and reaches threshold 1; this is the positive counterpart to the orc case.

Both ring recordings select one whole Ring_on file-port scope, not two separate source tasks. Include its other source branches and required consumed-return closure, remove replaced refusals, and wire the existing monster refresh with source-backed behavior. This does not grant completion credit to the whole accessory command or movement loop.
